content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"Marriage/bride imagery symbolizes the covenant union between God (or Christ) and His people: Christ as bridegroom, the Church as bride, built on the OT picture of Israel as YHWH's wife, culminating in the marriage supper of the Lamb. Alternatives concern who exactly the bride is (Israel, Church, New Jerusalem, individual soul), not the core marital-covenant symbolism.","book_summary":"Marriage/bride is the covenant union of God and His people — a one-flesh bond in which the wife receives the Husband's Name and comes under His covering; opposite is divorce.","consensus_core_identification":"Covenant marital union between God/Christ and His people (Israel/Church), with Christ as husband and the redeemed community as bride.","book_core_identification":"Covenant union of God and His people, characterized as a one-flesh bond involving name-taking and covering.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"None material. The book's broad formulation ('God and His people') encompasses both the OT Israel-as-wife imagery and the NT Christ-and-Church imagery, which the consensus explicitly treats as a unified tradition (Response C lists this synthesis as a common view). The added details of name-reception and covering are elaborations of the covenant mechanics, not boundary changes.","material_contradiction":"None. The book affirms the same central referent the consensus identifies; nothing in the entry denies the Christ-Church or Israel-YHWH identifications.","rationale":"Both readings reduce to the same minimum core: marriage symbolizes the covenant union of God with His people. The book's citation set (Gen 2:24 + Eph 5:31-32 one-flesh/Christ-and-church; Ezek 16:8 covenant with Israel; Rev 19:7 marriage of the Lamb) tracks exactly the texts the consensus responses use. The 'one-flesh bond,' 'covering' (Ezek 16:8's spread skirt), and name-reception are added texture describing the nature of the union rather than a changed referent or extension. The stated opposite (divorce) is a natural corollary, not a disagreement.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue REFINED because the book foregrounds distinctive covenant mechanics — the wife receiving the Husband's Name and coming under His covering — which the consensus does not emphasize, and because 'God and His people' flattens the consensus's Christ-Church specificity. But these are elaborations and a broader phrasing already present as a common consensus synthesis, not a change in extension or referent; also, the 'receives the Husband's Name' clause has no directly supporting citation among the printed verses, which is why support is judged partial rather than strong.","confidence":"high"}
